judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's positive findings all hold. I independently expanded every transformation, recomputed both composites, derived all four inverses and checked the domain reasoning: problem 6's f^-1(x) = (3x+1)/(x-2) with the domain/range swap note, problem 8's excluded input x = -3 arising from the inner output hitting f's bad input, problem 10's (f o g)^-1 = g^-1 o f^-1 shown both ways, and problem 12's branch selection justified by the restriction rather than by convention — all correct, and the two manual items (11b, 12a) carry genuine grading notes. Twelve problems are present and readable. What the judge did not check is the Quick Answers bank against the printed prompts, and by the standard this same judge applied to curr-403 and curr-404 in this run, this case has the same defect. Problem 3(a) prints 'Find f^-1(x)' and the bank prints '3. x, 5' — the 'x' is the output of verify.json's composition identity '2*((x+3)/2)-3' = x, not the requested formula (x+3)/2. Problem 6(a) likewise prints '6. x, 6.5' where (3x+1)/(x-2) belongs. Problem 12(b) prints '12. x, 5' where sqrt(x)+1 belongs. Problem 10 asks for (f o g)(x) = 2x+6 and its inverse and the bank prints only the single value x/2 - 3. Most concretely, problem 8 explicitly asks the student to 'state the one input value that f o g must exclude from its domain' — the answer x = -3 is a machine-checkable value that appears nowhere in verify.json and nowhere in the bank, which prints only '8. 0.5'. That is an uncovered, requested, checkable answer, not an open-response item. I therefore agree with ACCEPT on the mathematics and the instructional design, but the answer_key_quality 4 is generous relative to how the same bank defect was scored elsewhere in this run.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 9 is the standout item: 'For which value of x is f^-1(x) = 2? Answer without ever writing f^-1 if you can see the shortcut, then check with the formula.' The key teaches the reading f^-1(x) = 2 <=> f(2) = x and closes with 'Students who see that stop computing inverses they do not need.' It rewards a structural insight and still requires the mechanical check, in one item.

Problem 5's key does not stop at the expansion — it states the thesis the whole sheet is built on: 'composing with x + 4 on the inside is exactly the horizontal shift rule ... Transformations are compositions with simple linear functions.' The interleaving is justified mathematically rather than merely scheduled.

Problem 11 uses a two-row table (f(1) = 4, f(3) = -2) instead of a formula, and the key points out that only one of the two table entries is actually needed for h(2). The unused row is a deliberate discrimination test, and the manual grading note ties the wrong value -2 to the specific order error that produces it.

Problem 10's key explains the reversal with a concrete image ('the same reason you take your shoes off before your socks') AFTER deriving both sides algebraically, so the mnemonic sits on top of a proof rather than replacing one.

Both manual items are declared as type 'manual' in verify.json with descriptive text, and each has a matching 'Grading note (manual)' in the key stating what earns full credit and what does not — problem 12(a) explicitly rules out 'because we restricted it'.

root_causes.description: Every inverse-formula request on this sheet is verified by composing the claimed inverse back to x, and the bank prints that identity's expected value ('x') in the slot where the formula belongs. The formula itself is never a declared expected value, so it cannot reach the fast-grading column. Separately, problem 8's requested excluded-domain value has no verify entry at all, even though it is an ordinary machine-checkable number.
evidence: verify.json id 3: equiv '2*((x+3)/2)-3' expected 'x'; worksheet.pdf problem 3(a) asks 'Find f^-1(x)'. answer_key.pdf bank prints '3. x, 5'.
verify.json id 6: equiv '(2*((3*x+1)/(x-2))+1)/(((3*x+1)/(x-2))-3)' expected 'x'; bank prints '6. x, 6.5' where (3x+1)/(x-2) is the requested answer.
verify.json id 12: equiv '(sqrt(x)+1-1)**2' expected 'x'; bank prints '12. x, 5' where sqrt(x)+1 is requested.

worksheet.pdf problem 8 asks to 'state the one input value that f o g must exclude from its domain' (answer -3); verify.json id 8 contains a single eval at x = -1 and nothing else, and the bank prints '8. 0.5'.
worksheet.pdf problem 7(a) asks 'Write the rule for h(x)' (3*sqrt(x+4) - 1); verify.json id 7 has only the eval at x = 5, so the bank prints '7. 8'.

root_causes.description: The bank and the worked key disagree on the printed form of problem 6's evaluation. verify.json declares expected 6.5 as a float, which render_quick_answers.py formats by repr, so the bank shows 6.5 while the key's boxed answer is the exact fraction 13/2. A grader scanning the bank and a student reading the key see different-looking answers to the same question.
evidence: answer_key.pdf worked solution 6: 'Evaluating, f^-1(4) = 13/2, so f^-1(4) = 13/2' (boxed).
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt: floats are rendered with repr, so an exact rational declared as a float can never print as a fraction.

root_causes.description: Both of this sheet's manual items are attached to problems that also carry machine entries, and the bank shows no trace of the manual half. scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry collects only entries that have an 'expected' key and prints the manual em-dash solely when that list comes back empty, so a mixed problem renders exactly like a fully verified one.
evidence: verify.json id 11 contains an eval (expected -5) and a manual entry for the three-transformation description; answer_key.pdf bank prints '11. -5' with no manual marker.
verify.json id 12 contains a manual entry for part (a) plus an equiv and an eval; the bank prints '12. x, 5'.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry: the '---' fallback triggers only 'if not vals', which a mixed problem never reaches.

improvements.title: Declare the inverse formula and the excluded-domain value as verified answers, not just the composition identity that checks them
improvements.proposed_change: Add a response-slot inventory gate: every lettered sub-part and every conjoined request inside one must resolve to a verify entry whose expected value IS that response, or to a manual entry naming it. Give scripts/verify.py a symbolic answer type so an inverse formula can be a declared expected (checked by equivalence against the composition it already computes), and require an explicit entry for excluded-domain values — problem 8's x = -3 is a plain number that today's contract simply never asked for. In SKILL.md state the rule directly: a composition identity of the form f(f^-1(x)) = x is a CHECK, and its expected value 'x' must never be the value that reaches the Quick Answers bank in place of the formula.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture built from curr-405 problem 3: a prompt with slots (a) 'Find f^-1(x)' and (b) 'evaluate f^-1(7)', with verify.json containing only equiv '2*((x+3)/2)-3' = 'x' and eval '(x+3)/2' at 7 = 5. tests/check_answer_key.py must exit non-zero naming the uncovered formula slot in problem 3 and must report 'x' as an identity byproduct occupying an answer position. Add a second fixture from problem 8 where the prompt asks for an excluded input value and no verify entry covers it; the gate must fail there too.
improvements.expected_impact: On this sheet alone it restores four missing inverse formulas and one missing excluded value to the grading column. Because the composition-identity-as-answer pattern is the same one that produced the hard failures in curr-403 and curr-404, the fix is shared across the run's dominant failure mode.
improvements.risk: Requires symbolic comparison for the added answer entries, which is looser than numeric equality and can accept an equivalent-but-differently-written formula; the bank must therefore print the author's literal declared string. The slot inventory will also need a manual override where a prompt phrases two requests in one clause.

improvements.title: Keep the bank's numeric form identical to the key's boxed form (13/2, not 6.5)
improvements.proposed_change: Disallow bare JSON floats for exact rational answers in verify.json — accept a string expected such as '13/2' and render it through the same exact-form path used for symbolic values, or have render_quick_answers.py rationalise a float whose exact form appears in the key. Add a consistency check to tests/check_answer_key.py comparing each bank cell against the boxed answer in the corresponding worked solution and failing when the two render differently.
improvements.regression_test: Assert that a verify entry whose exact answer is 13/2 and whose key box prints 13/2 produces a bank cell reading 13/2 rather than 6.5. The assertion fails on today's renderer, which reprs the declared float.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a small but repeated grader-facing inconsistency where the fast column and the worked key show the same value in two notations; matters most on precalculus sheets where exact form is itself part of the expected answer.
improvements.risk: Some answers are genuinely decimal by request (curr-404's three-decimal item), so the rule must distinguish 'exact value declared as a float' from 'decimal approximation deliberately requested', which needs an explicit approx type rather than inference from the number's shape.

improvements.title: Show a manual-review marker on Quick Answers rows that mix machine-verified and manual entries
improvements.proposed_change: Change scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry so a problem whose entry list contains any type == 'manual' appends an explicit marker to its row, instead of the current behaviour where the manual em-dash is reachable only when the problem has no machine entries at all. Add a legend line under the bank so the glyph is self-explanatory on a printed key.
improvements.regression_test: Render curr-405's verify.json id 11 (one eval expected -5 plus one manual entry) and assert the bank row carries a manual marker. It renders as bare '-5' today, so the assertion fails before the fix. Assert a manual-only problem still renders the plain em-dash so existing behaviour is preserved.
improvements.expected_impact: A teacher grading from the bank can see that problems 11 and 12 are only half finished by the machine — currently the two items carrying the sheet's assessed reasoning look fully answered.
improvements.risk: Adds width to bank rows and may push the adaptive column count down on dense sheets; the marker should be a single glyph rather than a word.

case_summary: A strong interleaved-synthesis set: twelve problems that treat transformation, composition and inversion as one idea, with an explicit thesis (a transformation is a composition with a linear map) that problem 5 demonstrates and problems 9, 10 and 12 exploit. I verified every result independently and found no mathematical error; both manual items are properly declared and carry usable grading notes. The ACCEPT is deserved on mathematics and design. My one substantive divergence from the judge is that the Quick Answers bank has the same coverage defect this run treated as a hard failure elsewhere: all four requested inverse formulas are replaced by the composition identity's expected value 'x', problem 7's requested rule for h is absent, and problem 8's requested excluded input x = -3 is neither verified nor printed despite being an ordinary checkable number. A minor form inconsistency also exists between the bank's 6.5 and the key's boxed 13/2. None of these change the verdict, but they are the same reusable gap and should be recorded against the same issue key rather than lost because this case passed.
